descriptionChirho: The physical substance of the human (or animal) body, flesh as material reality. This encompasses several closely related sub-uses: the physical body as created by God ('the two shall become one flesh,' Matt 19:5-6, Mark 10:8), the mortal human condition ('all flesh' = all living beings, Matt 24:22, Mark 13:20, Luke 3:6), the incarnation of the Word ('became flesh,' John 1:14), flesh and blood as markers of human mortality and limitation ('flesh and blood did not reveal this,' Matt 16:17), the physical body of the risen Christ ('a spirit does not have flesh and bones,' Luke 24:39), and the born-of-flesh/born-of-spirit contrast in John 3:6. Also includes the Johannine eucharistic language of eating Christ's flesh (John 6). The Pauline theological extension where 'flesh' denotes the unregenerate human nature or sinful impulse (Rom 7-8, Gal 3:3, 5:13-24) arises naturally from this physical sense through metonymy and is not a separate lexical entry but a contextual theological development. All four clusters represent the same word across different grammatical forms and contextual nuances.
